info.name: CBPay API
info.description:
CBPay is a multi-currency payment platform: fiat payouts and collections
across Latin America, internal transfers, on-chain USDT funding and
withdrawals, and KYC screening â€” all against a single USDT-denominated
balance per account.

All amounts are decimal strings. Balances are held in USDT with 6 decimal
places. Errors always return `{"error": "<code>", "message": "<detail>"}`.

request.description:
Creates a person or company account with its owner login member and
returns a session token. One endpoint for both types: `type` is data.
Login members of the calling account (company accounts).
Adds a login member. Only available for company accounts.

Issues a server-to-server API key bound to the calling account. The
plaintext token (`pk_...`) is returned exactly once and cannot be
retrieved again.

request.description: Immutable ledger history of the calling account.

item.name: Get my FX rates and fees

request.description: Returns the exchange rate that applies to the calling account for each country — the same rate used when operations execute (`local_amount / rate = USDT`) — plus the account's fee configuration so clients can compute net prices.
Returns the payouts of the calling account.

Disperses fiat to a local bank account. The local amount is converted
to USDT at the current rate; `usdt_amount + fee` is debited and held
until the dispersal completes. If it fails, the full debit is refunded.

Requires an idempotency key (body field or `Idempotency-Key` header).
Retrying with the same key returns the original payout (`200` with
`idempotency_hit: true`).

response.name: 200 Idempotency replay of an existing payout.
response.status: Idempotency replay of an existing payout.

request.description:
Available payout corridors (country, currency, method) offered by
CBPay. Pass-through of the processing core catalog.

Creates an active fiat charge (e.g. a QR) through the processing core.
When the payment arrives, the account is credited automatically in
USDT (gross at FX rate, minus the payin fee) and the
`payin_credited` webhook fires.

Moves USDT between two CBPay accounts, atomically and always free of charge — any combination works: person to person, person to company, company to person or company to company. The destination is resolved by `to_account_id` or `to_email`. The recipient's webhook subscribers receive `transfer_received`.

Sends USDT on-chain. `amount + withdrawal fee` is debited atomically
and held; final state arrives via the
`crypto_withdrawal_status_changed` webhook. `failed` refunds the full
debit.
Funding credits and withdrawals of the calling account.
Returns every wallet of the calling account, oldest first.

Creates a new on-chain USDT wallet for the calling account. Person accounts hold **one wallet per network**; company accounts can create **unlimited** wallets per network (use `label` to tell them apart).

Every creation bills the `wallet_creation` fee when configured by CBPay (fixed per wallet; 0 = free, the default; configurable per account). The charge is refunded automatically if creation fails.

Verifies the calling account's identity — KYC for persons, KYB for companies (detected from the payload) — against the compliance service. If a compliance fee is configured, it is debited before the call and refunded if the screening fails. The response includes the screening result plus `kyc_status`, `compliance_service` and `compliance_fee`.

response.name: 201 Screening submitted; account KYC status set to `pending`.
response.status: Screening submitted; account KYC status set to `pending`.

request.description: Re-runs the account's verification. Requires a prior KYC/KYB submission. Bills the `compliance_rescreen` fee if configured; refunded on upstream failure.
Toggles continuous compliance monitoring for the account's verified identity. Enabling bills the `compliance_monitoring` fee if configured; disabling is free. Requires a prior KYC/KYB submission.

Subscribes an HTTPS callback to the calling account's events.

Deliveries are signed: `X-Webhook-Signature = hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + body))` with the timestamp in `X-Webhook-Timestamp`. Up to 5 attempts with incremental backoff.
Public liveness check of the API and its database.
